solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Speed head of police found in bust at quarters

indicators.note: a thing found in another sits inside it, so the police's first letter goes inside the word for bust

parts.note: a police raid is a bust

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the four quarters of the compass are North, East, South and West; here N, E, S, S

explanation.surface: A senior police officer is discovered at someone's quarters during a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts P, the head of 'police', inside RAID; the compass quarters N, E, S, S follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidness is quickness of motion, a plain synonym for speed.

clue.text: Chap originally from America supporting game

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath the part it holds up

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: A man who first came from the USA backs a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' sets F plus US below RU in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rufus is a man's given name, and a chap is any man.

clue.text: Accomplices miscreants initially employed in foreign prince's terrain

indicators.note: something employed in a scheme is put to work inside it, so a letter goes within the mixed letters
foreign suggests the letters are made strange, rearranged into a new order
initially means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Wrongdoers are hired to work in the land belonging to an overseas royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges PRINCES TERRAIN, and 'employed in' sets M, from 'miscreants initially', within that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Partners in a crime are those who collude in wrongdoing, which is what accomplices are.

clue.text: Comparatively dopey girl accepting arguments with hesitation

indicators.note: a word accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
rows are quarrels or arguments
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A rather dim young woman takes on disputes but falters.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsier is the comparative of drowsy, sleepy and dull-witted, a fair match for more dopey.

clue.text: Current disturbance in which donkey loses head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: neddy is a British pet name for a donkey

explanation.surface: Something upsets the flow, in which a donkey is beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the N of NEDDY, a British nickname for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl that disturbs the run of water or air, a disturbance in a current.

clue.text: Unexpectedly see pretty old printing plate

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out in a surprising arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Out of the blue, you spot an attractive antique plate used by printers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' mixes SEE PRETTY with O for 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a solid metal plate cast from a mould of set type, used in printing.

clue.text: Old coin and key dropped in tube

indicators.note: something dropped in a container falls inside it

parts.note: a duct is a tube or channel
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: An antique coin and a key have fallen down a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped in' puts A, a musical key, inside DUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin formerly used across Europe.

clue.text: Catch sight of man on call

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: Des is a man's name, short for Desmond
a cry is a call or shout

explanation.surface: Spot a man who is telephoning.
explanation.definitionFit: To descry is to discern or make out something at a distance, so to spot it.

clue.text: Precise reference cathedral clergy note in poetry of our era?

parts.note: the chapter is the body of canons who run a cathedral

indicators.note: one piece put in another sits inside it

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks dates of the current era
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: The cathedral's clergy observe that there's poetry written in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N for 'note' inside AD, 'of our era', making the little word between the two longer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Citing book, section and line, as with Bible texts, gives an exact source, so the idiom means precise detail.

clue.text: Tutor disturbed by start of rebellious youth's initial disloyalty

indicators.note: a word disturbed by a letter has it intruding into its middle

parts.note: a tutor is a teacher

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
a word's initial is its first letter

explanation.surface: A teacher is troubled by a rebellious youngster's first act of betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed by' puts R, the start of 'rebellious', into TEACHER; Y, 'youth's initial', ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery is betrayal of trust, the same as disloyalty.

clue.text: Give up protecting virtuous head? How could you?

indicators.note: a word protecting others wraps around them

parts.note: to forsake is to give up or abandon
good means virtuous
a ness is a headland or promontory, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Abandon a guard of a saintly leader? What were you thinking?
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a leader here but a headland, a ness; 'protecting' splits the word for give up around the two inner pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exasperated exclamations of reproach at someone's behaviour.

clue.text: Hospital in Paris is most sound

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
est is French for is, so 'is' as it would be said in Paris

explanation.surface: There's a hospital in the French capital that is the healthiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sane means of sound mind, so the superlative means the most rational.

clue.text: Unstable northern union leader dressed in blue?

indicators.note: a letter dressed in a word is clothed by it, sitting inside

parts.note: blue means risqué or sexually explicit

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shaky northern trade union boss wears blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' sets U, the union's leader, inside EROTIC, 'blue' in the sense of smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurotic person is anxious and emotionally unsteady, hence unstable.

clue.text: A universal god's joint contribution to literature

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
Thor is the Norse god of thunder; the possessive gives the S
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A god known everywhere sends a shared piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorship is the act of writing a book, a writer's own contribution to literature.

clue.text: Permanence of ill repute — shame about that

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a shame, as in what a pity, is a pity

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A lasting bad name — what a pity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' turns 'repute' into ERPETU, and 'about' has the shame word go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpetuity means everlasting duration, the state of being permanent.

clue.text: Long drink containing very soft fruit

parts.note: to pine is to long for

indicators.note: a word containing another holds it inside

parts.note: ale is a drink
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very soft

explanation.surface: A tall drink with very soft fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb, to yearn; 'containing' signals the musical marking going inside the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit with a tough spiky rind.

clue.text: Female leaves instruction to barrister to make cheese

indicators.note: when a letter leaves a word it is taken out

parts.note: a brief is the instructions a solicitor gives a barrister

explanation.surface: A woman quits a case and turns to cheesemaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes F, 'Female', from BRIEF; a barrister is a British courtroom lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Visiting Irish county, see Scottish beef producer

indicators.note: something visiting a place goes inside it

parts.note: Galway is a county on the west coast of Ireland
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Visiting an Irish county, look at a Scottish cattle breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is the old exclamation of 'look!', and 'Visiting' puts it inside the county on Ireland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Galloway is a hardy black beef cattle breed from south-west Scotland.

clue.text: This is nothing without a form of security

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the word goes around the a

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Without one thing, a security measure is worth nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: NIL goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail fastens things securely in place, one way of making something secure.

clue.text: Tea leading pair of Cypriots served outside simple priest's office

indicators.note: served outside means placed around, so the tea and the two letters go either side of the plain word
leading means going in front of what follows

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: a pair of means the first two letters of the word

parts.note: plain means simple

explanation.surface: Tea is served outdoors to a couple of Cypriots before a modest clergyman's service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' takes two letters of 'Cypriots'; with the tea 'leading' they make CHACY, which 'served outside' wraps around the word for simple.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplaincy is the post or office held by a chaplain, a priest serving an institution.

clue.text: Short words many ultimately used for formal greeting

parts.note: curt means short or brusque

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Many people use brief words as a formal way of saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives the last letters of 'words' and 'many', S and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtsy is a bob made by bending the knees, a respectful greeting to royalty.

clue.text: Bill loses third of money, having soldiers to equip

indicators.note: a word that loses a letter has it taken out

parts.note: an account is a bill

indicators.note: third of means the third letter of the word money

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: An invoice drops part of the cash, having troops to kit out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes N, the 'third of money', from ACCOUNT; RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To accoutre is to dress or fit out, especially with military gear, so to equip.

clue.text: Fragrant spices Charlie is very fond of

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to love is to be very fond of

explanation.surface: Charlie adores aromatic seasonings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloves are dried aromatic flower buds used as a spice.

clue.text: Place of depravity old bikers get upset over entering

indicators.note: something entering a word goes inside it
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: mods were 1960s British youths on scooters

explanation.surface: Elderly motorcyclists get annoyed about being let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get upset over' turns MODS, scooter-riding 1960s British youths, to SDOM; 'entering' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed for its wickedness, a byword for a den of vice.

clue.text: Like listeners — 11? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means leaving out the front half of the word, keeping only its back four letters

parts.note: 11 refers to the answer at 11 across, an eight-letter word

explanation.surface: Like listeners to the anxious type? Not a bit of it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' drops the first half of the 11-across answer, leaving its last four letters. 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic means relating to the ear, and ears are what listeners use.

clue.text: Working in Perth, wanted to celebrate uninhibitedly

indicators.note: working means being worked on, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: While employed in a Scottish city, someone wanted to let their hair down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges all the letters of IN PERTH WANTED TO; Perth is a city in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go out on a wild spree of partying, celebrating without restraint.

clue.text: Coarse rock some may remember on reflection

indicators.note: reflection is a mirror image, so the hidden letters read backwards
some means only part of the words, hidden within them

explanation.surface: Some people might recall a rough stone after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' hides YREME in 'may remember', and 'on reflection' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a dark granular rock ground up as an abrasive, as on nail files.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type, my padre, crazy about church

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go around the church
crazy means wild or deranged, so the letters are put in a mad order

explanation.surface: My priest, a thick-skinned fellow, is mad about the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' mixes MY PADRE into PAYDERM, and 'about' puts it around CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pachyderms are large thick-skinned mammals like elephants; the word is also used for an insensitive person.
